title: In 1960, Mathematicians Predicted that Earth’s Population Would Reach Infinity on a Friday Next Month - Nautilus
author: Jake Currie
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHistoryIn 1960, Mathematicians Predicted that Earth’s Population Would Reach Infinity on a Friday Next MonthIt will notJCBy Jake Currie1:00 PM CDT on October 8, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleIn 1960, a paper published in Science offered a grim prediction: the rapidly exploding human population would reach infinity on Friday, November 13, 2026, resulting in the extinction of humankind. According to the authors, who modeled future hyperbolic growth based on the last two millennia of data, it wasn’t a dearth of resources that would spell our doom, but something much more uncomfortable. “Our great-great-grandchildren will not starve to death,” mathematician Heinz von Foerster et al. wrote. “They will be squeezed to death.”Of course, unless you’re reading this from under a growing pile of your fellow man, it seems we’ve averted the apocalypse.
